requirements.requirement: Persist C.UTF-8 as the default locale for new login sessions on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent environment contains LANG=C.UTF-8, a clean login shell reported C.UTF-8, and both configuration and behavior remained present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Persist C.UTF-8 as the default locale for services on node1.
requirements.summary: OpenRC's global configuration exports LANG=C.UTF-8. A freshly restarted chronyd process inherited it, synchronization recovered, and the service retained the locale after a full node reboot.

overall_summary: Both material locale outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, observed a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and demonstrated recovered services, locale configuration and behavior, SSH listeners, and time synchronization.
limitations: Service locale inheritance was directly sampled only with chronyd; applicability to other OpenRC services is supported by the global /etc/rc.conf setting rather than additional process samples.
The generic lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it used systemctl on Alpine, although direct OpenRC checks showed the relevant services healthy before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations were appropriately limited to the locale configuration, bounded service validation, and mandatory reboot. The only unnecessary mutation was the reboot redirection file /tmp/[REDACTED].log created by cmd-479693fe00134e8e; it remained after completion and was absent from the baseline. This was minor, low-risk residue. Package health remained unchanged and expected SSH exposure recovered.
